newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-KIRSTEN MAKES INDIA PAY FOR SPILLING CATCHES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KIRSTEN MAKES INDIA PAY FOR SPILLING CATCHES.

text.p: Gary Kirsten made India pay for missed chances by scoring an unbeaten 86 by tea on the opening day of the second test on Thursday.
The South African opener, dropped on nought and seven by Mohammad Azharuddin and Anil Kumble off Venkatesh Prasad, made the most of his "lives" to guide his team to 168 for two.
India's only success of the afternoon session came with the dismissal of Adam Bacher for a confident-looking 25. He gloved an attempted hook off Javagal Srinath to wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia.
At 89 for two South Africa might have been vulnerable but Daryll Cullinan was smoothly into his stride before India spurned another chance.

Cullinan had stroked his way to 33 when he mistimed a drive at Doda Ganesh which VVS Laxman in the covers was unable to lay a hand on as he dived to his right. Cullinan had moved to 35 not out at tea.
India's sole reward of the morning session went to the deserving Prasad. He had Andrew Hudson caught behind for 16.
